page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2.0 threads per core. The memory configuration consists of 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. This server does not include any local storage or onboard GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance scoring 61847.21 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 16569.0. Memory bandwidth is also robust, recording 292.88 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 135.25 GB/sec for large block write operations. The processor's instruction set extensions, including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration, contribute to strong performance in Passmark CPU extended instructions and encryption tests.

While multi-core performance is strong, single-core benchmarks fall into the average category. Additionally, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it less suitable for memory-intensive applications, and the lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy machine learning tasks, as evidenced by a weak 2.77 tokens/sec in large 70B LLM text generation. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy, memory-lean workloads. It is best suited for software compilation, static web serving, multi-threaded decompression, and database operations.
